column7: Two holders of WithAuditCheckpointLock after a silent lock loss (docs/design/pooler-lock-loss.md row 15): the slower one, which read the floor before the faster one wrote a higher mark, no longer writes its lower high-water mark over it. advanceAuditHighWater (and the key-transition re-sign of the mark) write with CompareAndSetSystemMetadata on the value read; a lost write re-reads the floor and skips or retries once. Proved with two cores on separate pools, SQLite and PostgreSQL. Not covered: a DB-level actor who rewrites the row (ADR-029 residual; the signature and the checkpoint trail cover that); admin audit accept-loss still upserts, under the exclusive database lock with the server stopped.
